approved: Therapeutic Goods Amendment (2013 Measures No. 1) Bill 2013

Moved a bill giving the Health Minister power to exclude products such as bacteria-infused mattresses or power band bracelets from regulation as therapeutic goods, allowing the department secretary to remove non-therapeutic products from the register, and creating a new offence for providing false or misleading information when varying a product's registration.

Spoke on the Therapeutic Goods Amendment bill, which would give the minister power to exclude products such as holographic 'power bands' and bacteria-infused mattresses from the therapeutic goods regulatory scheme where public health risk is low, while still leaving them subject to consumer protection law.

Responded that the Therapeutic Goods Amendment bill would harmonise regulatory rules across different classes of therapeutic goods, noting the act's broad definition, unchanged for more than 20 years, increasingly catches products like mattresses and jewellery making health claims.
